textbookText: Observe the pictures given below and discuss the following questions.

i. What could be the organisms shown above? ii. Have you ever seen these organisms anywhere else? iii. Are they unicellular or multicellular? iv. Which kingdom do they belong to? v. Are they beneficial or harmful to us?

The organisms shown in the picture above are Euglena, Paramecium, Fuligo and Plasmodium respectively. Euglena is a microscopic, unicellular and flagellate organism primariely found in freshwater. Paramecium is also a microscopic and unicellular ciliate found in freshwater rich in decaying organc matter. Fuligo is a fungi like unicellular organism which can be seen in decaying woods. Similarly, Plasmodium is an intracellular blood parasite. Euglena exhibits both autotrophic and heterotrophic mode of nutrition as it can prepare its own food and sometime derives food from other micro-organisms whereas Paramecium is a heterotrophic because it derives food from other microorganism or organic substances. These organisms belong to the kingdom protista.

Kingdom protista (Gr; protistos, first of all) was proposed by Ernst Haeckel in 1866. Later, an American taxonomist Robert Harding Whittaker broadly divided all the living beings of this universe into five kingdoms in 1969 basically on the basis of phylogenetic relationship among them.
